examples.question_text:
A bag holds $4$ blue, $7$ yellow and $5$ white counters. One counter is chosen at random.
(a) Find $P(\text{yellow})$ as a fraction in simplest form.
(b) Explain why the answer is not $\frac{1}{3}$.
examples.solution_text:
(a) $4+7+5=16$ counters in total.
$P(\text{yellow})=\frac{7}{16}$
(b) Count counters, not just colours. The three colours have different numbers of counters, so they do not have the same chance.

examples.question_text:
Eight separate cards carry the letters of NOTEBOOK. A card is chosen at random.
(a) Find $P(O)$ as a fraction in simplest form.
(b) Find the probability of drawing O or B, as a fraction in simplest form.
(c) Separately, cards numbered $23$ to $37$, inclusive, are shuffled and one is drawn. Find the probability of an even number greater than $30$, as a fraction in simplest form.
examples.solution_text:
(a) The three O cards are favourable. There are $8$ cards.
$P(O)=\frac{3}{8}$
(b) The favourable cards are O, O, O and B.
$P(\text{O or B})=\frac{4}{8}=\frac{1}{2}$
(c) There are $37-23+1=15$ cards.
The cards satisfying both conditions are $32,34,36$.
$P(\text{even and greater than }30)=\frac{3}{15}=\frac{1}{5}$

(a) There is $1$ card numbered $6$ out of $8$ equally likely cards.
$P(6)=\frac{1}{8}$
(b) The favourable cards are $1,3,5,7$, so there are $4$.
$P(\text{odd})=\frac{4}{8}=\frac{1}{2}$
